title: Azzattiwadas
draftNote: Sign identifications and readings follow the Annotated Corpus of Luwian Texts and are checked against the Unicode sign list; individual readings remain scholarly judgments.
source: KARATEPE 1 (the Azatiwada inscription), Hieroglyphic Luwian version, copy Hu., clauses §22–§37. Text (transcription and sign-by-sign transliteration) follows the Annotated Corpus of Luwian Texts, ACLT 2 (I. Yakubovich et al., luwian.web-corpora.net), with sign identifications per the Unicode Anatolian Hieroglyphs repertoire (Laroche numbering); lemma meanings checked against open scholarly literature. The inscription survives in duplicate copies at the citadel's two gates (Hu. and Ho.); §17 is not preserved in either copy as the corpus gives them Transliteration conventions: Hawkins-style values as adopted by ACLT (the city name of clause 2 read Hiyawa; others read Adanawa). The stone's word-divider strokes and sign reversals are not reproduced. The original runs boustrophedon (alternating direction line by line) in registers of vertically stacked signs; it is presented here left-to-right and linear, with the corpus's recorded line divisions shown as ‖ marks. Translations are made fresh from the Luwian for this edition. Pronunciation convention: conventional scholarly Iron Age Luwian values (z = ts, h = a rasped kh).

images.caption: Blocks of the Hieroglyphic Luwian text at Karatepe's south gate, still standing where Azatiwada set them. The signs run in horizontal bands, each band read in the opposite direction from the one before.
images.alt: Stone blocks carved with bands of Anatolian hieroglyphs, set in a wall on a wooded hilltop
images.author: Klaus-Peter Simon

sentences.l: And I, Azatiwada, put them for myself under (my) feet.

morph.gloss: Azatiwada — here sounded Azzattiwara-, d heard as r
foot (classified by the foot sign PES)

sentences.i: And I, Azatiwada, set them beneath my feet.
sentences.n: A new movement opens with a full clitic chain hung on á-mu ammu 'I': =pa (the topic shifter — 'and as for …'), =wa, =mu 'for me' and =ada 'them', the last two squeezed into -ma-tà (the corpus leaves an unresolved query mark at the end of the chain). Watch the name: its ending is written with the ligature wa/i+ra/i — Azzattiwaras, the d of §1's Azzattiwadas heard as r between vowels. This d-to-r slide recurs throughout this part. padanza 'feet' is a dative plural under the foot classifier PES; INFRA-na-na is annan 'under', spelled as in §21; PONERE-há 'I put' is the logogram plus the 1st singular past ending -ha.

sentences.t: 𔕰𔕸𔓁𔑯 𔓤𔗲𔑯𔖪𔗷 𔐓𔕸𔑯𔖪 𔔉𔓶𔖱𔓵𔑶 𔗷𔑯 𔔘𔖻𔓶
sentences.l: Indeed in those places I built fortresses within,

morph.gloss: fortress (classified by the fortress-wall sign CASTRUM) — here neuter plural accusative

sentences.i: And in those very places I built fortresses,
sentences.n: kwippa ('indeed', a clause opener) carries =wa and =tta, the place particle. Two dative plurals in -nza agree: allantanza abattanza 'in those places' — the first written with the logogram LOCUS 'place' before its sound signs, the second the demonstrative aba- 'that'. harnissa 'fortresses' (neuter plural accusative) has the fortress-wall classifier CASTRUM, as in §19, and AEDIFICARE+MI-ha 'I built' repeats §19's verb; anta 'in' points back to the places.

sentences.l: by which Hiyawa dwells at ease.

morph.gloss: at ease, in comfort (classified by the BONUS sign; meaning approximate)
sit, dwell (SOLIUM, with its attached mi)

sentences.i: through which Hiyawa lives at ease.
sentences.n: kwadi is the relative kwi- in the instrumental, 'by which' — the purpose the fortresses serve. Hiyawa is the subject (nominative -s) with =wa after it and the city classifier at the end; the corpus glosses the name 'Que', the Assyrian name for the same Cilician kingdom, while this edition keeps Hiyawa (see §2). The verb asai 'dwells' is present 3rd singular, written with the seat logogram SOLIUM (asa- 'sit, dwell') and the small mi-sign that regularly rides with it. The BONUS sign before warriyamalla 'at ease' is a classifier; the word is rare and its exact nuance approximate.

sentences.l: And I destroyed strong(?) fortresses toward the west,

morph.gloss: fortress (the fortress-wall sign CASTRUM as logogram) — neuter plural accusative
strong(?) — the corpus takes it here as an adjective agreeing with 'fortresses'; meaning uncertain
the sunset, the west (classified by OCCIDENS) — dative

sentences.i: And I tore down mighty(?) fortresses to the west,
sentences.n: The verb comes first: L274-ta-li-ha 'I destroyed', with L274 — a sign scholars still cite by its list number — standing for the opening of hattal(a)i- 'destroy'. The spelling runs on -há-wa/i, just like latrahha=ha=wa in §5 (=ha 'and' + =wa); the corpus's transcription prints only hattaliha, so treat the reading of those last two signs as this edition's (the copy at the other gate writes hattaliha=wa). CASTRUM is now the word itself, with -sà for its ending. allummidaya, under the fist sign, is §19's rare word, parsed here as an adjective 'strong' in the neuter plural accusative agreeing with the fortresses — the meaning is still a guess. OCCIDENS is a classifier on ibami 'the west' (dative).

sentences.l: which the foremost kings had not destroyed,

morph.gloss: 3rd person plural past — '(they) destroyed' (the n goes unwritten)

sentences.i: ones that the earlier kings had not destroyed —
sentences.n: na 'not' (NEG₂, as in §21) leads with =wa; kwaya is the relative kwi- in the neuter plural accusative, 'which (fortresses)'. hattalainta is 3rd plural past (-nta, the n unwritten), with L274 now demoted to a classifier before a fully spelled word. Its subject comes last, nominative plural -nzi twice: FRONS 'front' + -li, hantili- 'foremost, earlier', and REX-ti, hantawatti- 'king', as in §2.

morph.gloss: 3rd person plural past — '(they) were' (the n goes unwritten)

sentences.i: the kings who came before me.
sentences.n: A short relative clause on those kings. ammu, the same form as 'I', is here the dative — 'before me', with parran 'before' (the logogram PRAE plus -na). kwinzi is the relative kwi- in the common plural nominative, 'who'; asanta '(they) were' is 3rd plural past. This copy has no =wa here — a rare clause without it (the copy at the other gate has ammu=wa).

morph.gloss: quotative particle + 'them' (=ada, sounded =ara) — fused in one ligature sign
Azatiwada — here sounded Azzattiwara-, d heard as r

sentences.n: The chain of §22 once more — ammu=pa=wa — but now the ligature wa/i+ra/i carries both =wa and the clitic 'them', =ada sounded =ara: two clitics in one sign. The name again ends in wa/i+ra/i (Azzattiwaras). L274 is a classifier here, in front of a fully spelled hattaliha 'I destroyed' (1st singular past -ha).

morph.gloss: them + the place particle — a whole clitic chain hiding in one modest spelling
lead, bring (here) (classified by the foot sign PES)

sentences.n: INFRA here stands for zanta 'down', not annan 'under' as in §22: one sign can carry related words, and the -ta after it shows which. The chain zanta=ha=wa=ada=tta ends in a single -ta that covers both =ada 'them' and the place particle =tta, as in §13. The foot sign (PES) classifies usa- 'lead (here)'; -ha is 'I' in the past.

sentences.t: 𔐿𔑯𔓶𔗬𔐫 𔕐𔓯𔑶𔖿𔓟 𔖖𔓛𔖻 𔐛𔐤 𔐓𔖻𔓱𔖪𔑯 𔓸𔓯𔖱𔓟𔖪
sentences.l: and them down I settled toward the east, at my borders.

morph.gloss: seat, settle — 'make sit' (classified by the seat sign SOLIUM)
border, frontier (classified by the boundary sign FINES)

sentences.i: and settled them toward the east, along my frontiers.
sentences.n: The same opening as §29, but here the final tà spells =ada 'them' alone. isnu(wa)- 'settle' — literally 'make sit' — takes the seat sign SOLIUM as its classifier. The east, kistami (dative), is written ORIENS-mi with the divine classifier DEUS before it; 'at my borders' is ammiyanza=tta irhanza, dative plural -nza on both words, with the boundary sign FINES classifying irh- 'border'.

sentences.t: 𔕰𔕸𔗬 𔐓𔗢𔗬𔓵𔖩𔔂 𔖩𔐫 𔐓𔕸𔑣𔓯 𔐿𔑯 𔕐𔓯𔑶𔖿𔗬𔓶
sentences.l: Indeed Hiyawans then I settled down there.

morph.gloss: seat, settle — 'make sit' (classified by the seat sign SOLIUM)

sentences.i: And then I settled Hiyawans there.
sentences.n: Three little adverbs: zira 'then' (spelled zi-tà, the d sounded r as in Azzattiwaras; the corpus files the word under the lemma zila), abadi 'there', and zanta 'down' by INFRA-ta again. Ahhiyawanninzi is the adjective 'Hiyawan' (common plural accusative -nzi) standing as a noun: 'Hiyawans'. The verb is 'I settled' once more, this time spelled with the -wa- of isnuwa-.

sentences.t: 𔗷𔗬 𔐓𔖻𔖪 𔖓𔓶𔔹𔓱𔖪 𔐓𔗢𔗬𔓵𔖩𔔂 𔓸𔗒𔖩 𔑁𔓊𔖹𔓶 𔖩𔐤 𔖬𔕸𔖻 𔐛𔓱𔐤 𔖩𔕸𔗬 𔓛𔑯𔖻 𔐛𔐤
sentences.l: And in my days I extended the Hiyawan borders, on this side toward the west, and on that side toward the east.

morph.gloss: extend, widen (classified by the hand sign)
on this side (paired: zin … zin=pa 'on the one side … on the other')
but, and on the other hand (contrast clitic)

sentences.i: In my days I pushed Hiyawa's borders outward, both westward and eastward.
sentences.n: A close echo of §5: latra- 'extend' under the hand classifier, and zin … zin=pa 'on this side … on that side'. a=wa opens the clause (a is a plain connective, 'and'); 'in my days' is amminza halliyanza, dative plural. irhinzi 'borders' (common plural accusative) is written FINES+HI — the logogram with the syllable it ends in tied on. OCCIDENS and ORIENS are now logograms in their own right, each followed by sound signs for the word's end (-pa-mi, -ta-mi).

sentences.t: 𔐓𔕸𔑯𔖪𔕸𔗬𔑯 𔓤𔗲𔑯𔖪 𔓶𔕸𔗬 𔕰𔓱 𔘰𔑶𔑯 𔑳𔗬𔐤 𔐓𔗔𔑯
sentences.l: And in those places which formerly were fearsome,

morph.gloss: and — in signs the corpus marks as erased or superfluous
topic shifter — in signs the corpus marks as erased or superfluous
quotative particle — in signs the corpus marks as erased or superfluous
3rd person singular past — 'was' (a neuter plural subject takes a singular verb)

sentences.i: And in those places that had once been feared,
sentences.n: A long frame of place: abattanza=pa=wa=tta allantanza 'in those places', dative plural as in §23 (the corpus marks its reading of the LOCUS sign as uncertain). The stone then repeats -ha-pa-wa/i; the corpus sets these signs in double angle brackets, as erased or superfluous — they are shown here but not translated. kwaya kwissanta 'which (were) fearsome' is neuter plural nominative, and its verb asta is singular: in Luwian a neuter plural subject takes a singular verb. kwissant- is spelled with hwa/i, a sign for the hw/kw sound; ruwan means 'formerly'.

sentences.l: where a man for himself fears to go the road,

morph.gloss: man, person (written with the head sign CAPUT; the corpus leaves the Luwian word open — §1 and §20 read the sign ziti-)
quotative particle + =di 'for himself' (3rd singular reflexive dative, sounded =ri) — fused in one ligature sign
go (classified by the walking-feet sign PES₂)

sentences.i: where a man is afraid to go along the road —
sentences.n: CAPUT-ti-sa is 'a man', nominative -s (the corpus writes it CAPUT-tt(i)-, leaving the Luwian word behind the head sign open, and glosses it '(noble)man'; §1 and §20 read the sign ziti-, but the double t of the corpus's form makes that uncertain here, so the logogram is left unvoiced). Its chain is packed again into wa/i+ra/i: =wa plus =di, the 3rd singular reflexive dative, sounded =ri — 'fears for himself', that is, is afraid. kwittan 'where' joins this to §33's places. kwissai 'fears' is present 3rd singular; harwan 'road' is an accusative (-n) on the road sign VIA; iuna 'to go' is an infinitive, under the walking-feet classifier.

sentences.t: 𔕰𔕸𔗬 𔗷𔖻𔓱𔖪 𔖓𔓟𔔹𔓱𔖪 𔑘𔑣𔖩𔓟 𔕗𔓉𔖹 𔑦𔑦𔐫𔑣
sentences.l: Indeed in my days women too walk with the spindle.

morph.gloss: spindle (classified by the spindle sign FUSUS)
instrumental ending — 'with' (the sign tara/i also carries the stem's last syllable)
walk, pass along — written with two walking feet; the Luwian word behind the picture is unknown
3rd person plural present — '(they) walk' (the n goes unwritten)

sentences.i: In my days women too walk about with their spindles.
sentences.n: Every word here is built from grammar already met: kwippa=wa, then the dative plural 'in my days'. The subject is FEMINA-ti-zi, wanatti- 'woman' in the nominative plural -nzi — the same woman sign that wrote 'mother' in §3 — with =ha 'and', here best felt as 'too'. sittari is sitta- 'spindle' in the instrumental, 'with the spindle', under the spindle classifier FUSUS. The verb is a pair of walking feet, PES₂.PES₂, whose Luwian reading is unknown; -danti marks the 3rd plural present, 'they walk'. Set against §34: on roads a man feared to travel, women now walk about with their everyday handwork.

sentences.t: 𔗷𔗬 𔐓𔖻𔓱𔖪 𔖓𔓟𔔹𔓱𔖪 𔒂𔖱𔖢𔖱𔗦 𔒈𔓟𔗦𔗦𔓶 𔗔𔐤𔗬𔖪𔗔𔓶 𔕐𔖻𔓱𔗔 𔗦𔑯
sentences.l: And in my days there were abundance and satiety(?) and very good living.

morph.gloss: abundance, fullness — written under the horn sign, the overflowing horn (meaning approximate)
satiety(?), luxury(?) — classified by the licking-mouth sign; the nuance is a scholarly guess
3rd person plural past — '(they) were' (the n goes unwritten)

sentences.i: In my days there was plenty and fullness(?), and life was very good.
sentences.n: An echo of §6: suri- 'abundance' under the horn sign (here the ligature CORNU+RA/I) and hassa- under the licking mouth (the corpus glosses it 'luxury'; the nuance is approximate, kept as in §6). Four nominatives in -s follow, linked by two =ha 'and'; sanawizzas (sannawizz(a/i)- 'very good'; the wa/i sign leaves a or i open) goes with asiyas 'living', written with SOLIUM.MI — the 'sit, dwell' sign again. The verb asanta '(they) were' is plural this time and is spelled without its first vowel (sá-ta).

sentences.l: And at ease dwelt Hiyawa and the Adanawan plain.

morph.gloss: at ease, in comfort (BONUS+RA/I; meaning approximate)
Adanawan, of Adana (classified by the city sign URBS)
neuter singular nominative ending, agreeing with 'plain'
territory, open land (TERRA+LA+LA) — the corpus's lemma; reading and meaning uncertain. §5's warra- 'plain' is spelled differently (wa/i+ra/i)

sentences.i: Hiyawa lived at ease, and so did the plain of Adanawa.
sentences.n: warriyamalla 'at ease' returns from §24, now with the logogram BONUS+RA/I standing for its opening, and carrying =ha=wa. asatta 'dwelt' is 3rd singular past, though Hiyawa (nominative -s) and the plain together are its subject. Here the city of Adana is spelled out in sound signs, á-ta-na-wa/i — Attanawanza, 'Adanawan', neuter singular nominative agreeing with the plain — beside the name sign *429 for Hiyawa. The land word is TERRA+LA+LA-za: the corpus transcribes it warranza but files it under walilid(a)- 'territory' — the two la signs fit that lemma better than §5's warra-, spelled wa/i+ra/i, so this may be a different word. Its reading is uncertain; 'plain' keeps §5's English.

glossary.(PES₂.PES₂)da-: walk, pass along — written with two walking feet; the Luwian word behind the picture is unknown
glossary.-di: ablative-instrumental ending — 'from, because of; by, with'
glossary.-i: two unrelated endings spelled alike: on nouns, the dative-locative singular — 'to, for, upon'; on verbs, the 3rd person singular present — '(he, she, it) …s'
glossary.-n: accusative singular ending — marks the object
glossary.-nta: 3rd person plural past ending — '(they) …-ed', '(they) were' (the n is usually left unwritten)
glossary.-nti: 3rd person plural present ending — '(they) …' (the n is usually left unwritten)
glossary.-nza: two endings spelled alike: the dative-locative plural — 'to, for, in, at' ('in my days', 'in those places'); and the neuter singular nominative/accusative ending of a noun or of an adjective agreeing with it
glossary.-nzi: common-gender plural ending, nominative or accusative
glossary.-s: nominative singular ending — marks the subject
glossary.-ta: 3rd person singular past ending — '(he, she, it) …-ed', 'was'; a neuter plural subject also takes it ('there were')
glossary.-ya: two endings spelled alike: on nouns, the dative-locative singular — 'to, for'; on neuter nouns, adjectives and pronouns, the nominative/accusative plural ('good things', 'which')
glossary.=ada: them (clitic pronoun, accusative plural; leans on an earlier word)
glossary.=ada=tta: them + the place particle — a whole clitic chain hiding in one modest spelling
glossary.=ha: and (clitic — glued to the end of its word)
glossary.=mu: me, to me, for me (clitic pronoun, leaning on the first word of the clause)
glossary.=pa: but, and; marks a new topic or a contrast — 'and as for …' (clitic; the corpus's =ba)
glossary.=tta: particle of place/motion — untranslatable filler in English
glossary.=wa: quotative particle — hangs on the first word of nearly every clause, marking the running narration; you'll see it constantly
glossary.=wa=ada: quotative particle + 'them' (=ada, sounded =ara) — fused in one ligature sign
glossary.=wa=di: quotative particle + =di 'for himself' (3rd singular reflexive dative, sounded =ri) — fused in one ligature sign
glossary.Ahhiyawanni-: Hiyawan, of Hiyawa — the kingdom in the Cilician plain
glossary.Attanawanni-: Adanawan, of Adanawa (Adana) — classified by the city sign URBS
glossary.Azzattiwada-: Azatiwada — the ruler who speaks this inscription (his name may mean 'beloved of the Sun'); between vowels the d may be sounded r (Azzattiwaras)
glossary.CAPUT-tt(i)-: man, person — written with the head sign CAPUT; the corpus leaves the Luwian word open (§1 and §20 read the sign ziti-)
glossary.allummida-: a rare word under the fist sign PUGNUS, meaning uncertain — the corpus takes it as an adjective, 'strong'; it may also be read as a noun, 'strong places'
glossary.ammu: I; also the dative 'me', 'to/before me' (spelled á-mu, or with the pointing-figure sign EGO)
glossary.asa-: sit, dwell (written with the seat sign SOLIUM and its attached mi)
glossary.asiya-: living, dwelling — a noun written with SOLIUM.MI, the 'sit, dwell' sign
glossary.hantili-: foremost, first, earlier (written with the FRONS 'front' sign)
glossary.harnissa-: fortress (written with or classified by the fortress-wall sign CASTRUM)
glossary.harwa-: road, way (written with the road sign VIA)
glossary.hassa-: satiety(?), luxury(?) — classified by the licking-mouth sign; the nuance is a scholarly guess
glossary.hattal(a)i-: destroy (written with the sign L274, as logogram or as classifier before the spelled word)
glossary.i-: go (classified by the walking-feet sign PES₂)
glossary.ibami-: the sunset, the west (written with or classified by the setting-sun sign OCCIDENS)
glossary.irhi-: border, frontier (written with or classified by the boundary sign FINES)
glossary.isnuwa-: seat, settle — 'make sit' (written with or classified by the seat sign SOLIUM)
glossary.kistami-: the sunrise, the east (written with or classified by the rising-sun sign ORIENS)
glossary.kwi-: who, which (the relative pronoun, written with the REL sign)
glossary.kwippa: indeed — adverb that opens a clause (the corpus's kwippa; the same spelling kwa/i-pa is written kwi=pa 'but, however' in §11)
glossary.latra-: extend, widen (classified by the hand sign)
glossary.pad(i)-: foot (classified by the foot sign PES)
glossary.sitta-: spindle (classified by the spindle sign FUSUS)
glossary.suri-: abundance, fullness — written under the horn sign, the overflowing horn (meaning approximate)
glossary.tu(wa)-: put, place (written with the PONERE sign)
glossary.usa-: lead, bring (here) (classified by the foot sign PES)
glossary.walilid(a)-: territory, open land — the corpus's lemma for the word written TERRA+LA+LA (transcribed warranza); reading and meaning uncertain
glossary.wanatti-: woman, wife (written with the woman sign FEMINA)
glossary.warriyamalla: at ease, in comfort (indeclinable; written with the BONUS sign, as classifier or as logogram; meaning approximate)
glossary.zanta: down (written with INFRA, as is annan 'under')
glossary.zila: then, thereupon (also sounded zira, the d/l heard as r)
glossary.zin: on this side (paired: zin … zin=pa 'on the one side … on the other')
